function: Channel acquisition for double-RIS: a conditional diffusion model generates the full cascaded channel from partial estimates, conditioned on the received pilot signal (p. 2-3).
system: Uplink: single-antenna user, BS with N=4 antennas, two passive reflecting RISs (M1=16-64 and M2=16-128 elements), direct link blocked; frequency band not stated (p. 2, 4, 5).
method: Conditional diffusion model with U-Net noise predictor, T=500 steps, conditioned on received pilot signal; trained with noise-prediction (denoising) loss on synthetic channels (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Synthetic cascaded double-RIS channels with spatial correlation sin(k)/k between RIS elements following [12]; training data from several simulated environments; no public dataset (p. 3-4).
test_conditions: Trained on synthetic channels from several environments; NMSE versus SNR (-5 to 20 dB), mask ratios 0.2 and 0.5, several RIS sizes; test set not described (p. 3-5).
baselines: LSTM estimator and CGAN, both learned; no non-learned estimator (LS, MMSE, compressive sensing) compared (p. 4-5).
metrics: NMSE between generated and ground-truth cascaded channel, versus SNR, array size and mask ratio (p. 4-5).
complexity: None; only a qualitative remark that larger arrays increase the computational burden (p. 5).
openness: None; no code or data link, synthetic data (p. 1-5).
q1_support: p. 1: "trained on synthetic channel data" - custom simulator with a spatial correlation model from [12] (p. 4); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 4: "We evaluate the NMSE performance of the doubleRIS system under different numbers of array elements" - sweeps of array size, SNR and mask ratio; the paper does not say that a model trained for one configuration is tested on another or adapted.
q3_support: p. 4: "we also incorporate the long short-term memory (LSTM) estimation algorithm and a representative deep learning method," the CGAN - both baselines are learned; Figs. 3-4 (p. 5) show no non-learned estimator, although the abstract (p. 1) claims to outperform traditional channel acquisition methods.
q4_support: p. 5: "which substantially increases the computational burden" - only a qualitative remark about array size; no complexity order, operations, parameters or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 1: "trained on synthetic channel data" - simulated data from a custom model; no code or data link or DOI is given and no public dataset is used.
notes: Included, area 2: channel generation and estimation of the double-RIS cascaded channel from partial pilot observations. The text extraction lost part of p. 5 (some paragraphs, the conclusion and the references), so I read p. 4-5 from the page images. The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint; it prints no DOI, so the match with the DOI could not be checked from the text.
